newsitem.title: UK: Orange lampposts head for London.
newsitem.headline: Orange lampposts head for London.

text.p: British mobile telephone operator Orange Plc said on Thursday its latest disguise for telecom masts -- lampposts -- had rung up so much support it was bringing them to London.

Having unveiled in February Europe's first telecoms mast that looked like a tree -- at least from a distance -- the group said its first lamppost mast had been used in the western English city of Bristol and had had no complaints.
"Funnily enough it looks like a lamppost," group technical and operations director Colin Tucker told a news conference following Orange's half year results.
"You will see Orange lampposts in London," he added.

In an effort to quell mounting criticism by environmentalists keen to block a tide of telecoms masts marching across the countryside and past garden gates, Orange is eager to develop new ideas and might even consider hiding its masts in sculptures.
The pressure on cellular operators to erect masts to boost national coverage is mounting because regulators want to discourage a proliferation of the 15-metre high, lattice transmitters after 1998.

Orange has about 2,900 sites, which it plans to increase by 6,000 by the first quarter of 1999 and more thereafter. Some 80 percent of its sites are on rented property. Of the remaining free-standing towers, it shares about one third with other operators.
Orange earlier beat expectations by slashing pre-tax half year losses 41 percent to 74 million pounds.
